question: Which law allowed inter-caste and inter-religious marriages during the British period in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Act of 1872**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Act of 1872, also known as the **Special Marriage Act of 1872**, was enacted during British India to allow civil marriages between individuals of different castes and religions.
 
• It provided a framework for inter-caste and inter-religious marriages without the need for conversion or adherence to personal religious laws.
 
• The Act required individuals to renounce their religious practices temporarily and marry under a secular framework.
 
• This was a significant step towards promoting social reform and addressing caste and religious barriers in Indian society.
 
• The Act served as the precursor to the **Special Marriage Act of 1954**, which governs civil marriages in independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Widow Remarriage Act (1856):**

 
 
• This Act was introduced by Lord Dalhousie and passed by Lord Canning in 1856.
 
• It legalized the remarriage of Hindu widows and aimed to improve the social condition of women in India.
 
• The Act was a progressive step influenced by reformers such as **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**.
 
 
 
• **Sarda Act (1929):**
 
 
• Also known as the **Child Marriage Restraint Act**, it was passed in 1929 to curb the practice of child marriage in India.
 
• The Act set the minimum age of marriage for girls at 14 years and for boys at 18 years, later revised to 18 and 21 years, respectively.
 
• It was spearheaded by **Harbilas Sarda**, a social reformer and judge.
 
 
 
• **Act of Settlement (1781):**
 
 
• This Act was passed by the British Parliament to settle disputes regarding the jurisdiction of courts in British India.
 
• It clarified the roles and functions of the Supreme Court of Calcutta and the East India Company’s judicial system.
 
• It did not pertain to social or marital reforms but rather focused on legal and administrative matters.
